INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the difference between hearing and listening? (1 mark)
   A. Hearing needs effort but listening does not
   B. They are exactly the same
   C. Hearing is only for adults
   D. Listening is done on purpose and hearing happens by itself

2. What is the plural of the English word loaf? (1 mark)
   A. loaf
   B. loaves
   C. loafes
   D. loafs

3. Which of these is a cultural food word? (1 mark)
   A. porridge
   B. window
   C. ruler
   D. pencil

4. Which words show the order of steps? (1 mark)
   A. sun, rain
   B. first, then, next
   C. red, blue, green
   D. mother, father

5. Why should instructions be clear? (1 mark)
   A. So nobody listens
   B. So people are confused
   C. So the listener can do the right thing
   D. So they are longer

6. What is intonation? (1 mark)
   A. The spelling of words
   B. The size of letters
   C. The number of words
   D. The rise and fall of the voice

7. Which of these must always begin with a capital letter in English? (1 mark)
   A. The names of colours
   B. The names of people
   C. The names of foods
   D. The names of weather

8. Which sentence uses a comma correctly for speaking to someone? (1 mark)
   A. Wanjiku please bring the, umbrella.
   B. Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.
   C. Wanjiku please, bring the umbrella
   D. Wanjiku please bring, the umbrella.

9. The word I is always written (1 mark)
   A. as a small letter
   B. as a capital letter
   C. with a comma
   D. in brackets

10. Which question word asks about a place? (1 mark)
   A. When
   B. Who
   C. Why
   D. Where

11. Why should you look back at the dialogue when answering questions? (1 mark)
   A. To find accurate answers
   B. To copy a friend
   C. To waste time
   D. To hide the page

12. What is the best way to read your part in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Never practise
   B. Read other people's lines
   C. Practise your lines with the right feeling
   D. Read it very quickly

13. Which sentence belongs to the main idea Fire is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. The market is far.
   B. Maize is tasty.
   C. Never play with matches.
   D. Rain is wet.

14. In the metaphor Time is money, what is the meaning? (1 mark)
   A. Time is valuable and should not be wasted
   B. Clocks are coins
   C. Time is made of paper
   D. Money is a clock

15. What is a tongue twister? (1 mark)
   A. A phrase that is hard to say fast
   B. A kind of drum
   C. A very long word
   D. A silent poem

16. Which comma use is correct? (1 mark)
   A. When the bell rang we, ran.
   B. When, the bell rang we ran.
   C. When the bell, rang we ran.
   D. When the bell rang, we ran.

17. Which strategy would you use to find a price in an advert? (1 mark)
   A. Drawing
   B. Scanning
   C. Singing
   D. Skimming

18. What should you check when you reorder jumbled words? (1 mark)
   A. That the sentence makes sense and has a verb
   B. The paper
   C. The colour of the letters
   D. Nothing

19. Which is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. A pen
   B. I bought a pen.
   C. The red pen.
   D. I saved money, so I bought a pen.

20. What does change mean in a shop? (1 mark)
   A. The weather
   B. The clothes
   C. Money given back after paying
   D. A journey

21. The goat is inside the shed. Which preposition shows this? (1 mark)
   A. behind
   B. in
   C. between
   D. outside

22. Who should you call for a sick animal? (1 mark)
   A. A veterinary doctor
   B. A driver
   C. A tailor
   D. A shopkeeper

23. Why should a writer plan a story before writing? (1 mark)
   A. To organise the ideas
   B. To skip the ending
   C. To lose the ideas
   D. To avoid a title

24. Which is NOT a feeling shown by interjections? (1 mark)
   A. Disgust
   B. The price of an item
   C. Pain
   D. Joy

25. How long should each line in a dialogue usually be? (1 mark)
   A. None
   B. Short, like real speech
   C. Very long speeches
   D. One page

26. Which device is used mainly to take photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Torch
   B. Camera
   C. Clock
   D. Radio

27. Which is the last part of a telephone conversation? (1 mark)
   A. Giving your name
   B. Asking for a favour
   C. Greeting
   D. Saying goodbye

28. What is a choral poem? (1 mark)
   A. A written test
   B. A poem performed by a group together
   C. A map
   D. A silent poem

29. Does every poem have to rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. Only short poems
   B. Yes, always
   C. No
   D. Only long poems

30. What should the title of an instruction chart do? (1 mark)
   A. Be blank
   B. Hide the task
   C. Tell what the task is
   D. Give a joke

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three good manners to show when collecting proverbs from an elder. (3 marks)

32. After listening to a safety story, describe how you would answer four kinds of comprehension questions and give one example of each. (5 marks)

33. What is a vocabulary bank and why is it useful? (2 marks)

34. Give two reasons why we read fluently. (2 marks)

35. Give two examples of constructive leisure activities. (2 marks)

36. Describe what an imaginative composition is. (2 marks)

37. Read: Mama Wanjiru buys tomatoes, an onion and three cabbages at the market. List the nouns and say which are singular and which are plural. (5 marks)

38. Describe how a class can start a reading club. (4 marks)

39. Explain why pace matters when reading a poem. (3 marks)

40. State three rules for a debate. (3 marks)

41. State three steps for building vocabulary from a text. (3 marks)

42. Match each interjection with its feeling: (a) Hurray (b) Yuck. (2 marks)

43. Describe your favourite leisure activity using the who, where, when and why frame. (3 marks)

44. List three note points from a passage about a kite on a free day. (3 marks)

45. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about today's weather. Use at least one comma in a list, two capital letters for names and three full stops. (5 marks)

46. Join with but: The trader was tired. He kept working. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Listening is done on purpose and hearing happens by itself
   Hearing happens naturally, but listening is a choice to pay attention.

2. B — loaves
   Loaf changes f to ves in the plural.

3. A — porridge
   Porridge is a food. The others are not.

4. B — first, then, next
   Sequence words show the order.

5. C — So the listener can do the right thing
   Clear instructions prevent mistakes.

6. D — The rise and fall of the voice
   Intonation is voice movement.

7. B — The names of people
   Names of people and places begin with capital letters.

8. B — Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.
   A comma follows the name of the person addressed.

9. B — as a capital letter
   In English the word I is always a capital.

10. D — Where
   Where asks for the place.

11. A — To find accurate answers
   Answers should come from the text.

12. C — Practise your lines with the right feeling
   Practice with expression helps fluency.

13. C — Never play with matches.
   It is a detail about fire safety.

14. A — Time is valuable and should not be wasted
   The metaphor shows the value of time.

15. A — A phrase that is hard to say fast
   Tongue twisters train clear speech.

16. D — When the bell rang, we ran.
   A comma follows the when part at the start.

17. B — Scanning
   You know exactly what you need.

18. A — That the sentence makes sense and has a verb
   A sentence must make sense.

19. D — I saved money, so I bought a pen.
   It joins two sentences with so.

20. C — Money given back after paying
   Change is the money you get back.

21. B — in
   In shows something is inside.

22. A — A veterinary doctor
   Veterinary doctors treat animals.

23. A — To organise the ideas
   A plan gives the story shape.

24. B — The price of an item
   Interjections show feelings, not prices.

25. B — Short, like real speech
   Real conversations use short turns.

26. B — Camera
   A camera takes photos.

27. D — Saying goodbye
   Calls end with a goodbye.

28. B — A poem performed by a group together
   Chorus means together.

29. C — No
   Some poems do not rhyme.

30. C — Tell what the task is
   The title names the task.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet politely, listen without interrupting, ask permission to write, say thank you.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: Answer who with a person (his mother), what with an event (touched the pot), where with a place (the clinic) and why with a reason (he wanted to see the steam). Give short, full answers and ask for repetition if needed.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each kind and example, and one mark for full sentences.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is a class list of words on one theme. It helps pupils remember and use new words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the use.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps listeners understand and enjoy, and it helps the reader to understand the text.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each reason.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reading, sports, drawing, singing, gardening, community service (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: A story that comes from the writer's imagination and is not a true report.
   Working / marking points: One mark for story and one for imagination.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Nouns: Mama Wanjiru, tomatoes, onion, cabbages, market. Singular: Mama Wanjiru, onion, market. Plural: tomatoes, cabbages.
   Working / marking points: One mark for finding all five nouns, two marks for correct singular nouns and two marks for correct plural nouns.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect books, choose a name and a librarian, agree on rules for borrowing, meet regularly to read and share books, and record who borrowed each book.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: A pace that is too fast makes words unclear, and one that is too slow loses interest. A good pace helps listeners follow and feel the mood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of three ideas.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen without interrupting, speak politely, give reasons, accept the result graciously, take turns.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read once for meaning, underline new words, write them on flashcards with meanings, use each in a sentence (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) joy (b) disgust
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any clear description that says the activity, where and when it is done, with whom and why you like it.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for activity, place or time, and reason.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Children go to the field, fly a paper kite, string breaks, grandfather mends the kite (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each short correct note.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example On Monday in Kisumu the sky was cloudy. It was cool, windy and dry. Amina wore a sweater.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence that is complete and correct, one for a comma in a list and one for correct capitals.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: The trader was tired, but he kept working.
   Working / marking points: One mark for but, one for the comma, one for correct order.
